approved: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Supporting Retirement Incomes) Bill 2018

Moved an amendment supporting a bill that increases the pension work bonus income exemption to $300 a fortnight and opens the Pension Loans Scheme to full-rate pensioners at up to 150 per cent of the full pension rate, while condemning the Government's past push for pension changes that would have left pensioners $80 a week worse off.

The member supported the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Supporting Retirement Incomes) Bill 2018, welcoming the increase in the work bonus from $250 to $300 and the expansion of the Pension Loans Scheme to all Australians of age pension age, while calling for indexing the work bonus and for increasing the pension and introducing a dental voucher for pensioners, noting that half a million older Australians rely solely on the age pension and almost a third live in poverty.

The speaker supported the bill’s changes to increase the work bonus income exemption from $250 to $300 per fortnight and the income bank from $6,500 to $7,800, expand the Pension Loans Scheme to full-rate pensioners with a maximum payment of 150% of the full pension (up to $11,912 for singles or $17,958 for couples), and smooth means testing for pooled lifetime income streams, but criticised the Morrison government for past pension cuts—including attempts to cut indexation, increase the pension age to 70, and reduce concessions—and for delaying financial protections.

The speaker supported elements of the bill, including increasing the pension work bonus to $300 per fortnight and the work bonus income bank to $7,800, and expanding the Pension Loans Scheme. They criticised the government for past pension cuts, including a 2014 attempt to cut pension indexation by $23 billion and a deal with the Greens affecting 370,000 pensioners by up to $12,000 a year.

Supported the Supporting Retirement Incomes bill's three changes, expanding the Pension Loans Scheme and pension work bonus and adding a new means test rule for lifetime income products, and attacked Labor's franking credits policy, citing a local newspaper report that it would hit 5,500 retirees in his electorate for an average of $2,200 a year.

The speaker supported the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Supporting Retirement Incomes) Bill 2018, which increases the work bonus threshold from $250 to $300 per fortnight, extends the Pension Loans Scheme to all older Australians with securable real estate, and changes means testing for pooled lifetime income streams from 1 July next year. The speaker also argued that Labor’s proposed policy on imputation credits would constitute a "retiree tax" affecting 20,000 Tasmanians, citing constituent Mr Arnold Fanning, and claimed 97% of affected retirees have taxable incomes below $87,000.

The bill implements three measures from the 2018–19 budget: new means test rules for pooled lifetime income streams; an increase of the pension work bonus to $300 per fortnight, extended to self-employed; and an expansion of the Pension Loans Scheme to allow loans up to 150% of the maximum pension rate, all commencing 1 July 2019.
